anti_patterns: Do not turn an existing requirement for examples or counterexamples into a duplicate checklist with no search transformation.
Do not import empirical estimation, identification, regression, or data-fitting workflow into a theoretical probe.
failure_modes: A failed numerical search is misreported as proof that no admissible open region or mechanism exists.
The selected cases all occupy one local cell and conceal reversals elsewhere in the maintained parameter domain.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable when removed complexity is economically first-order or when simplification changes the solution concept.
The move must stop when numerical reliability cannot be separated from the economic structure being investigated.
operation_steps: Solve the smallest tractable cases and deliberately varied nearby instances while recording exact domains and solver assumptions.
Preserve strict crossings, perturbation margins, reversals, failures, and primitive-by-primitive ablations rather than selecting one sign.
Export only a candidate cutoff, ordering, statistic, equivalence, or functional form plus the analytic obligations needed to establish it.
moves.runtime_projection: Trigger when a general model is too opaque to reveal which primitives generate a result, or when an apparent effect may be a finite-case artifact. Construct the smallest tractable instances and solve deliberately varied nearby cases. Record strict crossings, perturbation margins, the exact tested domain, solver assumptions, and every reversal or failure. Remove primitives one at a time and search across cases for a cutoff, ordering, sufficient statistic, equivalence, or functional form. Export only that candidate structure and the analytic obligations needed to establish it. Finite or numerical evidence is never a universal proof, and the move is inapplicable when simplification removes a load-bearing institutional feature.
success_diagnostics: A strict witness survives a declared perturbation and suggests one interpretable structure that normal proof work can test.
The output preserves tested scope and counterexamples and does not upgrade numerical evidence into a universal statement.
trigger_conditions: The apparent effect may be a finite-cell artifact rather than a strict result on a nonempty open parameter region.
The general model is too opaque to reveal which primitive, cutoff, ordering, or statistic generates the candidate result.

anti_patterns: Do not presume that posterior, cutoff, continuation-value, or dual representations are inherently superior to the maintained objects.
Do not use lower dimension, mathematical elegance, or shorter notation as a proxy for scientific contribution quality.
failure_modes: A notation-only compression is treated as a new mechanism, theorem, or novelty contribution.
The new representation suppresses a load-bearing institution or silently narrows the feasible set, equilibrium, or claim domain.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable when the current representation is already minimal and exposes the mechanism without case enumeration.
The move must stop when the proposed map cannot preserve a researcher-owned primitive or other load-bearing institutional detail.
operation_steps: Re-express the same primitives through beliefs, likelihood ratios, cutoffs, continuation values, sufficient statistics, or dual objects.
Derive the map from the original formulation, state its losslessness conditions, and preserve the first compression failure.
Retain the representation only when it exposes an ordering, decomposition, comparative static, or transferable mechanism.
moves.runtime_projection: Trigger when the current model can be solved only by enumerating cases or when its mechanism remains hidden behind a high-dimensional state. Re-express the same primitives through a compact economic object: posterior beliefs, market-clearing cutoffs, continuation values, a sufficient statistic, or a dual variable. Derive the map from the original formulation, state the conditions under which it is lossless, and locate the first case where it fails. Keep the alternative only if it exposes an ordering, decomposition, comparative static, or transferable mechanism. If it merely shortens notation or suppresses a load-bearing institutional feature, return it as a diagnostic boundary rather than a promoted model.
success_diagnostics: The alternative representation preserves the maintained model and reveals an economic ordering, decomposition, or nearby transfer.
The first failed mapping is explicit enough to become a scoped boundary rather than disappearing behind new notation.
trigger_conditions: The current model can be solved only by enumerating cases and has no recovered primitive ordering or low-dimensional economic object.
The mechanism remains hidden behind a high-dimensional state, notation system, or application-specific formalization.

anti_patterns: Do not use analogy as a novelty verdict or as a replacement for closest-theory, proof, interpretation, or human investment review.
Do not add capacity, congestion, endogeneity, or another research object merely to rescue a weak or absorbed current mechanism.
failure_modes: Shared labels or mathematical form are mistaken for a primitive-level structural map.
The first formal mismatch is promoted despite leaving every prediction, mechanism, feasible object, and economic consequence unchanged.
moves.functional_name: Analogical Structure Transfer — First Mapping Failure
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable until one exact mechanism chain and one function-only comparator structure can be stated.
A mapping that requires a different research object must stop and surface the need for separate human reframe authority.
operation_steps: Map primitives, information, timing, feasible actions, strategic arrows, solution concept, and outcomes to one distant structure.
Mark each mapping exact, conditional, or failed and isolate the first economically load-bearing failure rather than shared vocabulary.
Construct the smallest variant isolating that failure and record which prediction changes relative to both structures.
moves.runtime_projection: Take one structurally distant model and write a one-to-one map from its primitives, information, timing, feasible actions, strategic-response arrows, solution concept, and outcome object to the current mechanism. Mark every mapping as exact, conditional, or failed. Ignore shared labels. Select the earliest economically load-bearing failure and construct the smallest variant that isolates it. Compare that variant with both the current benchmark and the source structure; record which prediction changes and why. Treat an exact mapping as absorption risk, not novelty proof, and a failed mapping as a conjecture, not a contribution. Return an analogy map, failure witness, minimal variant, and non-applicability note; do not choose routes or make investment decisions.
success_diagnostics: The map distinguishes exact common structure from one failure that changes a mechanism, prediction, feasible object, or consequence.
Exact mapping remains absorption-risk evidence and failed mapping remains a conjecture pending ordinary proof and novelty work.
trigger_conditions: Several proposals retain the same primitive-to-response chain under different labels or application nouns.
The candidate contribution may be a standard structure embedded in a new setting and its absorption boundary is unclear.

anti_patterns: Do not begin with a preferred formal model and invent a market operation merely to justify it.
Do not treat a technology label or implementation detail as an economic primitive without a participant-level consequence.
failure_modes: A long catalogue of institutional detail replaces one testable economic mechanism.
The changed rule affects terminology or software implementation but not information, actions, transfers, strategic response, or payoffs.
non_applicability: The move is unnecessary when the operative institution, ordinary benchmark, and strategic consequence are already explicit.
The move must stop when the only difference is a label, interface convenience, or detail outside the maintained economic object.
operation_steps: Reconstruct what each participant observes, searches, remembers, can commit to, can enter or exit, and how allocation and payment occur.
Choose the closest standard operating institution and replace exactly one inherited rule with the proposed primitive.
Trace the resulting change through feasible actions, beliefs or strategic responses to one allocation, price, rent, participation, liability, or welfare consequence.
moves.runtime_projection: Use this move when a topic is still carried by broad labels rather than a market operation. Reconstruct what participants observe, search, remember, can commit to, can enter or exit, and how allocation and payment occur. Choose the closest standard institution and replace exactly one operating rule. Trace that change through feasible actions, beliefs, and strategic responses to one price, allocation, rent, participation, liability, or welfare consequence. Reject details that only rename software or add realism without changing behavior. Return one institutional delta, ordinary-agent benchmark, mechanism chain, and concrete economic consequence.
success_diagnostics: One operative institutional difference generates a concrete strategic arrow and an economically interpretable consequence.
The ordinary-agent benchmark differs only in that operative rule, not in generic intelligence or computational power.
trigger_conditions: The proposed question is carried by broad labels such as AI, platform, identity, or information rather than an operative market rule.
The ordinary-agent benchmark and the strategic consequence of the new technology cannot yet be stated in institutional terms.

anti_patterns: Do not use the move as a novelty verdict or as permission to avoid ordinary literature and absorption work.
Do not replace the researcher-owned economic tension with a different question merely because it is easier to formalize.
failure_modes: A cosmetic extension is presented as a new question because the application noun or technology label changed.
Several primitives change together, so no economic source of the new prediction can be isolated.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable without one exact source mechanism and one substantive implementation difference.
The move must stop when the alternative changes the human-owned question or produces no behavioral or outcome difference.
operation_steps: State the source result as a function-only mechanism and preserve the original economic tension rather than its notation.
Change one substantive primitive, timing, information, commitment, or implementation rule and derive the first strategic arrow that differs.
Compare the changed prediction with both the original result and the ordinary institutional benchmark, retaining the first absorption failure.
moves.runtime_projection: Use this move when a nearby result is interesting but the current proposal adds only a label or cosmetic extension. State the source result as a function-only mechanism and preserve its economic tension. Change exactly one substantive primitive, timing, information, commitment, or implementation rule. Derive the first strategic response that differs and compare the resulting prediction with both the source model and the ordinary institutional benchmark. If the change is absorbed by notation or requires a different human-owned question, return that boundary. Output one implementation delta, mechanism comparison, prediction difference, and absorption risk.
success_diagnostics: One substantive implementation difference changes a strategic response, feasible object, prediction, or economic consequence.
The comparison explains why the result is not absorbed by the source model under a change of notation.
trigger_conditions: A nearby paper or standard result is interesting, but the current proposal adds only a label, application noun, or cosmetic extension.
A substantive implementation, timing, information, commitment, or institutional assumption could plausibly carry the result.

anti_patterns: Do not delete a rule merely because its origin is historical or because a simpler model is easier to solve.
Do not imitate a founder, import management style, or treat cross-domain success as economic validation.
failure_modes: Physical or technical feasibility replaces incentives, information, commitment, or institutional enforcement.
Minimalism removes the actual economic object, or elegance is treated as evidence of contribution quality.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable when the questioned institution is itself the research object or when removal changes the solution concept.
Cross-domain evidence cannot support the move unless two independent economic anchors preserve incentives and institutional meaning.
operation_steps: Freeze the economic puzzle and target consequence, then classify each inherited requirement as feasibility, information, incentive, commitment, institution, or convenience.
Rebuild the smallest coherent benchmark from defensible constraints and restore an omitted assumption only when its removal changes the feasible set, strategic response, prediction, or consequence.
Preserve the first failed removal, the minimal restored set, and the abandoned scaffold as explicit boundaries.
moves.runtime_projection: Use this move when a model inherits many requirements whose economic role cannot be explained. Freeze the researcher's puzzle and target consequence. Classify each requirement as feasibility, information, incentive, commitment, institution, or convenience. Rebuild the smallest coherent benchmark from defensible constraints, restoring an assumption only when its removal changes the feasible set, strategic response, prediction, or consequence. Preserve the first failed removal and the minimal restored set. Never replace incentives with physical feasibility, delete the institution being studied, or treat simplicity and cross-domain success as scientific validation.
success_diagnostics: The rebuilt benchmark isolates a smaller set of constraints that still generates the target mechanism and consequence.
A failed removal identifies a load-bearing economic assumption rather than merely preserving familiar notation.
trigger_conditions: The proposed model inherits several requirements or assumptions whose economic role and source cannot be explained.
The central puzzle is obscured by conventional scaffolding, yet removing assumptions indiscriminately could erase incentives or institutions.

anti_patterns: Do not add an endogenous state merely because dynamic models look richer than static benchmarks.
Do not change the researcher-owned question, welfare object, or solution concept without human approval.
failure_modes: A future institution is endogenized only to rescue a weak question, with no participant able to affect it.
The feedback adds many political or organizational objects without isolating one changed strategic response.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable when future authority and information are truly fixed by the maintained institution.
The move must stop when participants cannot affect the future state or the feedback requires a different research object.
operation_steps: Write one exact chain from the current rule through an endogenous power, information, participation, or commitment state to the future continuation response or reoptimization.
Feed the continuation response back to current incentives and compare it with a fixed-state benchmark plus a full-commitment benchmark whenever commitment is the proposed channel.
Construct the smallest two-period witness, preserving any offsetting response, persistence, and first failure boundary.
moves.runtime_projection: Use this move when a rule, designer, or institution is treated as fixed even though current behavior may alter who controls, observes, or chooses in the next period. Write one exact chain from the current rule through an endogenous power, information, participation, or commitment state to a future reoptimization, then feed that continuation response back into current incentives. Compare it with a fixed-state benchmark and, when commitment is the channel, a full-commitment benchmark. Build the smallest two-period example. Preserve offsetting responses and regime persistence. If future authority is actually fixed, participants cannot affect the state, or the added feedback changes the researcher-owned question, return a non-applicability boundary rather than manufacturing dynamics.
success_diagnostics: One current choice changes an explicit future state, the continuation is re-solved, and the closed feedback changes an ex ante strategy or produces a strict invariance.
The commitment benchmark and two-period witness separate a real dynamic mechanism from decorative extra timing.
trigger_conditions: A current rule or action plausibly changes who controls, observes, participates, or chooses in a later period.
The proposed mechanism treats a future institution or designer as fixed despite an economically stated feedback.

anti_patterns: Do not default to max-min preferences or worst-case design without an institutionally stated decision criterion.
Do not use robustness language as a substitute for closest-theory, economic interpretation, or novelty work.
failure_modes: An arbitrary huge uncertainty set makes the conclusion empty and is then presented as robustness.
Several assumptions change together, so the surviving or failed prediction cannot be attributed to one axis.
Worst-case mechanism performance and an across-information outcome envelope are merged into one ambiguous claim.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable when the uncertainty set has no economic or institutional basis.
The move must stop when the axis cannot be varied without changing the research question or several primitives together.
The move is outside scope when resolving the uncertainty requires empirical identification or estimation.
operation_steps: Select exactly one designer-knowledge or information axis and declare an economically justified set of alternatives.
Declare whether the operator is a worst-case guarantee or an across-structure outcome set, and never merge the two.
Recompute behavior while holding the question, payoff environment, solution concept, and all other primitives fixed.
Record the surviving prediction set, any simple institution that remains valid, and the first failure boundary.
moves.runtime_projection: Use this move when a result depends on the analyst or designer knowing an exact action set, technology, or private-information structure. Select one institutionally justified knowledge axis, declare the admissible alternatives, and choose either a worst-case guarantee or an across-structure outcome set; never merge the operators. Recompute behavior while holding the economic question, payoff environment, institution, timing, and solution concept fixed. Record the survivor, sharp outcome set, or first failure boundary and compare it with a narrower class. Do not vary several assumptions, treat a wider set as a stronger contribution, or import empirical identification. If the class has no economic basis, the move is inapplicable.
success_diagnostics: One defensible uncertainty-axis change and one explicit operator reveal a prediction that survives, a sharp outcome set, or an exact failure.
The output states which primitives stayed fixed and does not upgrade set width or worst-case performance into contribution.
trigger_conditions: A candidate result depends on exact knowledge of an action set, technology, or private-information structure.
The economic question is stable, but one knowledge assumption has no institutional justification and may drive the result.

anti_patterns: Do not make incentive compatibility a box-checking exercise detached from the candidate mechanism and equilibrium.
Do not silently invoke a revelation principle outside its maintained information, commitment, and equilibrium domain.
failure_modes: A preferred allocation is optimized before messages, incentives, participation, and feasible transfers are stated.
One failed implementation is misreported as proof that no mechanism can implement the researcher-owned outcome.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable until the desired outcome and equilibrium concept are stable enough to test.
The move must stop when there is no candidate implementation or when testing it would alter a human-owned primitive.
operation_steps: Fix the information, timing, messages, actions, transfers, participation, commitment, and equilibrium concept.
Construct the simplest direct or indirect mechanism and search for the first profitable deviation, refusal, infeasible transfer, commitment breach, or unintended equilibrium.
Preserve a minimal type-state witness and separate failure of the proposed implementation from failure of the economic question.
moves.runtime_projection: Use this move when a desired allocation, social goal, or intuitive mechanism is stated before the strategic path that could implement it. Fix the information, timing, feasible messages and actions, transfers, participation, commitment, and equilibrium concept. Construct the simplest direct or indirect mechanism, then search for the first profitable deviation, refusal to participate, infeasible transfer, commitment breach, or unintended equilibrium. Preserve a minimal type-state witness and distinguish failure of this implementation from failure of the economic question. Do not assume truth telling, optimize before feasibility, or infer global impossibility from one counterexample. Return the exact gap and the smallest repair obligation.
success_diagnostics: The move produces either a complete minimal strategic path or one exact implementation-gap witness.
The witness identifies the failed constraint without turning one counterexample into a universal impossibility claim.
trigger_conditions: A desired allocation, social goal, or intuitive mechanism is stated without an explicit strategic path that implements it.
Truth telling, participation, commitment, transfers, or the relevant equilibrium are assumed rather than demonstrated.

anti_patterns: Do not use a journal target, theorem density, or general vocabulary as a reason to alter the unit of analysis.
Do not overwrite a human-approved ResearchQuestion or disguise a new research objective as a harmless semantic reframe.
failure_modes: The branch quietly replaces the researcher-owned tension with a broader but different question and is presented as a continuation.
A fashionable label or higher level of abstraction is treated as wider contribution without a changed mechanism, prediction, or economic object.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable until the current tension, benchmark prediction, and decisive outcome can be held fixed across branches.
The move must stop when the only wider question requires a different human-owned objective, institution, welfare criterion, or empirical task.
operation_steps: Freeze the current economic tension, exact benchmark prediction, and decisive outcome before generating any alternative research branch.
Generate alternative units or objects of explanation and map, for each, what remains fixed and the first benchmark reasoning link that changes.
Retain only a branch that reveals a distinct mechanism or nearby transfer, and return it as a candidate requiring fresh human approval when the research question was already accepted.
moves.runtime_projection: Trigger when a model preserves a real economic tension but its question remains application-bound or is absorbed by a familiar benchmark. Freeze the tension, benchmark prediction, and decisive outcome. Generate alternative units or objects of explanation while holding those elements fixed. For each branch, state the first benchmark reasoning link that changes, the mechanism it reveals, and the nearby settings to which it could transfer. Retain only a branch that changes the economic object rather than labels, techniques, or venue rhetoric. Return candidate questions and a preservation map; changing an approved question still requires fresh human confirmation.
success_diagnostics: The candidate reframe preserves the original tension while identifying a different economic object and the first changed benchmark link.
The new branch has a stated consequence or transfer class that cannot be obtained by changing application nouns, notation, or venue rhetoric.
trigger_conditions: A real economic tension survives, but the current question is tied to one application label and is readily absorbed by a familiar benchmark.
The mechanism may matter beyond the current setting, but the unit or object of explanation prevents that transfer from being stated exactly.

anti_patterns: Do not treat approximation ratio, runtime, description length, or ease of proof as a proxy for economic contribution.
Do not suppress a load-bearing institutional detail or silently compare rules under different resources, objectives, or information structures.
failure_modes: Finite numerical closeness is reported as a universal approximation guarantee or as proof that the exact optimum is unnecessary.
The restricted class looks simple only because it changes the feasible set, objective, information instrument, or distributional benchmark.
non_applicability: The move is inapplicable when no exact benchmark and formal loss metric can be stated on the maintained environment.
The move must stop when the approximation gap swamps the economic consequence or the omitted complexity is institutionally first-order.
operation_steps: Fix the maintained environment, objective, feasible set, and exact optimum benchmark before choosing a simple economically interpretable class.
Prove an explicit additive or multiplicative loss bound, or an exact zero-loss implementation, and record every assumption supporting it.
Use a tight example and the first failure of the simple class to isolate the structure and load-bearing complexity that a stronger theorem must explain.
moves.runtime_projection: Trigger when an exact optimum is high-dimensional or distribution-specific and hides the mechanism. Fix the environment, objective, feasible set, and exact benchmark, then choose the smallest economically interpretable restricted class. Prove an additive or multiplicative loss bound, or an exact zero-loss implementation, and record every condition supporting it. Use the bound to isolate a cutoff, partition, monotonicity, sufficient statistic, or decomposition that a stronger theorem should explain. Stress the tight example and the first load-bearing complexity that defeats the simple class. Approximation without a formal guarantee or economic interpretation is inadmissible.
success_diagnostics: The candidate class has a nonvacuous formal loss bound or exact implementation and one transparent structure explaining the guarantee.
A tight witness and first failed assumption distinguish useful simplicity from omitted first-order institutional complexity.
trigger_conditions: The exact optimum exists but is high-dimensional, distribution-specific, or case-defined in a way that hides the economic mechanism.
A transparent restricted class may preserve most or all of the objective and expose a reusable cutoff, partition, ordering, or decomposition.

source_cards.citation: Hal R. Varian (1997), How to Build an Economic Model in Your Spare Time, The American Economist 41(2):3-10
does_not_support: The source does not claim that numerical examples prove universal results or that simplification should remove first-order institutions.
source_cards.functional_summary: The method essay explicitly recommends solving the simplest useful cases, comparing nearby examples, and simplifying before testing how far the discovered structure generalizes.
non_applicability: Do not simplify when the omitted institution or high-dimensional state is itself the economic object being explained.
source_cards.title: How to Build an Economic Model in Your Spare Time
source_cards.transferable_content: Use small cases to expose the operative pieces and errors, then export only the common candidate structure for general analysis.

source_cards.citation: Annie Liang (2026), Using Machine Learning to Generate, Clarify, and Improve Economic Models, accepted at Journal of Economic Literature
does_not_support: A computational pattern is not a theorem, economic mechanism, causal explanation, portability result, or evidence of reliable LLM novelty.
source_cards.functional_summary: The method article explicitly proposes predictive benchmarks and adversarial computational probes that locate model failures before human judgment turns patterns into interpretable economic structure.
non_applicability: Do not use a predictive or computational probe when no transparent outcome map exists or when solver error cannot be separated from economics.
source_cards.title: Using Machine Learning to Generate, Clarify, and Improve Economic Models
source_cards.transferable_content: Use transparent computational search to locate reversals, failures, or sensitive regions and retain the tested domain and assumptions.

source_cards.citation: José L. Moraga-González and Yajie Sun (2023), Product Quality and Consumer Search, American Economic Journal: Microeconomics 15(1):117-141
does_not_support: The final paper does not establish that its authors used computation to discover the result or that finitely many families prove universality.
source_cards.functional_summary: The published theory design preserves positive, negative, and ambiguous comparative-static cases while isolating conditions that organize their different signs.
non_applicability: Do not compare families that change the operative mechanism, suppress multiple equilibria, or remove load-bearing institutional detail.
source_cards.title: Product Quality and Consumer Search
source_cards.transferable_content: Vary an admissible family without changing the economic architecture, retain every reversal, and search for a general ordering or decomposition.

source_cards.citation: Emir Kamenica and Matthew Gentzkow (2011), Bayesian Persuasion, American Economic Review 101(6):2590-2615
does_not_support: The representation does not imply that all information problems are low dimensional or that it transfers without the paper's commitment structure.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper represents signal choice through posterior distributions and concavification, with explicit conditions for when belief-space dimension can be compressed further.
non_applicability: Do not impose posterior-distribution language when the original environment lacks the beliefs, commitment, or plausibility structure it needs.
source_cards.title: Bayesian Persuasion
source_cards.transferable_content: Search for a natural economic representation, derive the exact map and feasibility conditions, and record where dimensional reduction fails.

source_cards.citation: Eduardo M. Azevedo and Jacob D. Leshno (2016), A Supply and Demand Framework for Two-Sided Matching Markets, Journal of Political Economy 124(5):1235-1268
does_not_support: Cutoffs are not universal sufficient statistics, and continuum uniqueness does not transfer automatically to finite or frictional markets.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper represents stable matching through market-clearing cutoff vectors, making selectivity, equilibrium equations, and comparative statics more transparent.
non_applicability: Do not use the representation when stability, continuum, or market-clearing conditions are absent from the maintained model.
source_cards.title: A Supply and Demand Framework for Two-Sided Matching Markets
source_cards.transferable_content: Try a cutoff, price, or market-clearing representation only after deriving its exact relation to the original allocation problem.

source_cards.citation: Laura Doval and Vasiliki Skreta (2022), Mechanism Design With Limited Commitment, Econometrica 90(4):1463-1500
does_not_support: Canonical representation does not mean low dimensional, novel, or valid for arbitrary dynamic games and multi-agent commitment failures.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper uses posterior beliefs and a canonical mechanism class to make hidden information feedback explicit in a limited-commitment dynamic design problem.
non_applicability: Do not transfer the representation without the information, type persistence, and period-by-period commitment conditions that support it.
source_cards.title: Mechanism Design With Limited Commitment
source_cards.transferable_content: Represent an implicit informational state explicitly only when the map preserves the relevant equilibrium outcomes and constraints.

source_cards.citation: Yuliy Sannikov (2008), A Continuous-Time Version of the Principal-Agent Problem, Review of Economic Studies 75(3):957-984
does_not_support: Continuation value is not sufficient in every dynamic model, and continuous time is not generally superior to discrete formulation.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper uses continuation value as a recursive state that compresses history and exposes how incentive intensity and payment timing evolve.
non_applicability: Do not assume one-state compression beyond the maintained continuous-time agency environment; re-establish state sufficiency whenever its primitives change.
source_cards.title: A Continuous-Time Version of the Principal-Agent Problem
source_cards.transferable_content: Search for a recursive state or sufficient statistic, then state the conditions under which it preserves the original dynamic problem.

source_cards.citation: John William Hatfield, Scott Duke Kominers, Alexandru Nichifor, Michael Ostrovsky, and Alexander Westkamp (2019), Full Substitutability, Theoretical Economics 14(4):1535-1590
does_not_support: Formal equivalence is not novelty, and neither an arbitrary mismatch nor shared vocabulary is evidence of a useful new mechanism.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper maps substitutability concepts across several market languages and shows where economically meaningful trading-network features require a broader object.
non_applicability: Do not transfer definitions beyond the domain, preference, and choice-correspondence conditions under which their equivalence is shown.
source_cards.title: Full Substitutability
source_cards.transferable_content: Build an exact structural map across distant settings and treat the first economically load-bearing mismatch as a candidate boundary.

source_cards.citation: Stephen Morris, Hyun Song Shin, and Muhamet Yildiz (2016), Common Belief Foundations of Global Games, Journal of Economic Theory 163:826-848
does_not_support: The formal foundation does not transfer to arbitrary games and does not turn a generalization or application into a contribution automatically.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper maps special signal constructions to the deeper rank-belief properties driving selection and marks where binary symmetric scope stops transferring cleanly.
non_applicability: Do not import the mapping when action multiplicity, asymmetry, or population structure changes the belief property doing the work.
source_cards.title: Common Belief Foundations of Global Games
source_cards.transferable_content: Map the primitive or belief object that actually supports a result and record the first domain change that alters the prediction.

source_cards.citation: Kfir Eliaz and Ran Spiegler (2015), X-games, Games and Economic Behavior 89:93-100
does_not_support: Shared abstraction may indicate absorption rather than novelty, and the first formal difference is not automatically economically meaningful.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper maps distant applications to a common threshold and externality structure while preserving examples that fail to enter the formalism or change its equilibrium implications.
non_applicability: Do not use the analogy when threshold, continuity, or preference conditions erase the current mechanism or manufacture a false isomorphism.
source_cards.title: X-games
source_cards.transferable_content: Use a distant function-only comparator and preserve the first failed primitive or strategic arrow that changes a prediction.

source_cards.citation: Ariel Rubinstein (2006), Dilemmas of an Economic Theorist, Econometrica 74(4):865-883
does_not_support: The source neither bans formal analogy nor licenses a mapping or model result as prediction, policy advice, or novelty evidence.
source_cards.functional_summary: The essay treats simplified models as limited fables and preserves dilemmas about absurd conclusions, evidence, regularities, and real-world relevance.
non_applicability: Do not convert the skeptical boundary into a universal veto against abstract theory, formal comparison, or function-only transfer.
source_cards.title: Dilemmas of an Economic Theorist
source_cards.transferable_content: Use mapping failure as a boundary diagnostic while remaining skeptical that elegant structure, formal unity, or analogy establishes relevance.

source_cards.citation: Daron Acemoglu (2024), official Nobel Prize interview, recorded 6 December 2024
does_not_support: The interview does not establish novelty, correctness, or value for every alternative implementation.
It does not authorize imitation of a named scholar's personality or prose.
source_cards.functional_summary: The interview explicitly describes research ideas as byproducts of reading, real events, and asking how an existing paper might be approached differently, while emphasizing incremental science and repeated error checking.
non_applicability: Do not use the method when the alternative merely renames an existing object or changes a human-owned research question.
source_cards.title: Transcript from an interview with Daron Acemoglu
source_cards.transferable_content: Turn one encountered result or institution into a bounded alternative-implementation question, then test whether the changed primitive alters the mechanism rather than only its label.

source_cards.citation: Mark Armstrong and Jidong Zhou (2022), Consumer Information and the Limits to Competition, American Economic Review 112(2):534-577
does_not_support: The paper does not state a general research method or an AI-specific mechanism.
It does not imply that every information refinement is economically important.
source_cards.functional_summary: The theory design makes consumers' private preference information an operative market variable and traces how changing it alters differentiation, price competition, purchase allocation, and welfare.
non_applicability: Do not transfer the reconstruction when the changed detail alters no feasible action, information, transfer, strategic response, or payoff.
source_cards.title: Consumer Information and the Limits to Competition
source_cards.transferable_content: Reconstruct an apparently background operating rule as one exact information or action primitive and compare the resulting strategic response and economic outcome with the standard institution.

source_cards.citation: Alvin E. Roth (2002), The Economist as Engineer, Econometrica 70(4):1341-1378
does_not_support: The paper does not support importing every real-world detail into a model or replacing theory with engineering.
Successful implementation is not universal proof or a novelty verdict.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper argues that market design requires responsibility for institutional detail and shows how complications encountered in real design can generate new questions for economic theory.
non_applicability: Do not add institutional detail unless it changes a feasible, informational, strategic, transfer, or payoff object.
source_cards.title: The Economist as Engineer: Game Theory, Experimentation, and Computation as Tools for Design Economics
source_cards.transferable_content: Start from what a market actually asks participants to do, keep the smallest strategic complication that changes performance, and let that operative detail motivate a theory comparison.

source_cards.citation: Elon Musk (2008 interview; 2009 transcript), The Henry Ford Collecting Innovation Today oral history
does_not_support: The interview does not establish equilibrium, welfare, novelty, optimality, or scientific validity.
It does not support a universal deletion rule, economic authority, or imitation of management style and personality.
source_cards.functional_summary: The interview explicitly contrasts inherited convention with ground-up reasoning from well-supported fundamentals, while also noting that useful innovation must be better and often combines several interacting changes.
non_applicability: Do not transfer hardware reasoning without independent economic anchors, and do not remove incentives, information, commitment, or institutions merely because they are not physical constraints.
source_cards.title: The Henry Ford video oral-history interview with Elon Musk
source_cards.transferable_content: Separate hard constraints from inherited conventions, rebuild the smallest coherent system from defensible premises, and compare it with the inherited design without treating difference as value.

source_cards.citation: Daron Acemoglu and James A. Robinson (2008), Persistence of Power, Elites, and Institutions, American Economic Review 98(1):267-293
does_not_support: The paper does not imply that every formal reform is offset or that political power belongs in an unrelated research question.
source_cards.functional_summary: The theory makes de facto power an endogenous response to a formal institutional change, allowing strategic investment to offset the reform and generate institutional persistence.
non_applicability: Do not add institutional feedback when future authority is fixed or participants cannot affect the future state.
source_cards.title: Persistence of Power, Elites and Institutions
source_cards.transferable_content: Trace one current rule through an endogenous future power or authority state, solve the resulting continuation response or reoptimization, and feed it back to current incentives.

source_cards.citation: Gabriel Carroll (2015), Robustness and Linear Contracts, American Economic Review 105(2):536-563
does_not_support: The result does not justify arbitrary uncertainty sets, automatic max-min objectives, or general optimality of simple contracts.
source_cards.functional_summary: The model removes exact knowledge of the agent's action technology, declares the enlarged action uncertainty, and asks which contract remains optimal under that one change.
non_applicability: Do not use the reconstruction when the uncertainty axis has no institutional basis or changes several primitives at once.
source_cards.title: Robustness and Linear Contracts
source_cards.transferable_content: Remove one strong designer-knowledge assumption, state the economically admissible uncertainty set, and test which institutional prediction survives.

source_cards.citation: Dirk Bergemann and Stephen Morris (2013), Robust Predictions in Games with Incomplete Information, Econometrica 81(4):1251-1308
does_not_support: The analysis does not make all information structures equally plausible or a wider outcome set scientifically superior.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper separates the payoff game from private information and characterizes the equilibrium outcome set across admissible information structures, then shows how prior knowledge narrows it.
non_applicability: Do not vary information structures without an explicit admissible class and a maintained economic interpretation.
source_cards.title: Robust Predictions in Games with Incomplete Information
source_cards.transferable_content: Vary one explicit information-knowledge axis while preserving the payoff environment, and report the surviving prediction set and its first boundary.

source_cards.citation: Roger B. Myerson (1981), Optimal Auction Design, Mathematics of Operations Research 6(1):58-73
does_not_support: The paper does not license silent truth-telling, universal direct implementation, or auction regularity assumptions elsewhere.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper turns a seller's objective into an explicit game-design problem and optimizes only over feasible mechanisms subject to information, equilibrium, and incentive restrictions.
non_applicability: Do not transfer auction-specific virtual-value or independence conditions to a different mechanism environment.
source_cards.title: Optimal Auction Design
source_cards.transferable_content: Translate a desired outcome into an explicit strategic mechanism and expose feasibility, participation, equilibrium, and incentive conditions before optimization.

source_cards.citation: Eric S. Maskin (2007), Biographical essay, NobelPrize.org
does_not_support: The autobiography does not make one monotonicity condition universal or eliminate equilibrium-selection and feasibility requirements.
source_cards.functional_summary: The first-person account describes starting from whether a social goal can be implemented, searching for the property separating possible and impossible cases, and constructing a mechanism.
non_applicability: Do not invoke the method when no stable researcher-owned outcome or equilibrium concept has been specified.
source_cards.title: Eric S. Maskin - Biographical
source_cards.transferable_content: Begin from a desired outcome, identify the exact implementability condition, preserve impossibility, and pair any sufficient condition with a construction.

source_cards.citation: Simone Galperti, Aleksandr Levkun, and Jacopo Perego (2024), The Value of Data Records, Review of Economic Studies 91(2):1007-1038
does_not_support: The paper does not show that every marginal unit is insightful or that a reframed object is novel, important, welfare improving, or empirically measurable.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper holds information intermediation fixed while changing the unit of analysis to one data record, revealing a pooling externality across records and a portable marginal-value object.
non_applicability: Do not use this reframe when the proposed unit erases the original strategic interaction or changes the researcher-owned economic tension.
source_cards.title: The Value of Data Records
source_cards.transferable_content: Reframe a narrow question by changing its unit or explained object only when the original economic tension remains fixed and the new object reveals a distinct strategic channel or transfer class.

source_cards.citation: Xavier Gabaix (2014), A Sparsity-Based Model of Bounded Rationality, Quarterly Journal of Economics 129(4):1661-1710
does_not_support: The paper does not establish universal sparsity or license replacement of a faithful institution with a convenient behavioral operator.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper moves from anomaly-specific adjustments to a sparse decision operator that preserves standard benchmarks and transfers across demand and equilibrium questions.
non_applicability: Do not transfer the operator or the reframe without an exact benchmark map and the first benchmark reasoning link that changes.
source_cards.title: A Sparsity-Based Model of Bounded Rationality
source_cards.transferable_content: Change the object being explained rather than adding primitives, and retain the reframe only when it preserves the benchmark tension and generates a reusable mechanism across nearby settings.

source_cards.citation: Jason D. Hartline and Tim Roughgarden (2009), Simple versus Optimal Mechanisms, ACM Conference on Electronic Commerce:225-234
does_not_support: The paper does not justify arbitrary constant-factor approximation or transfer auction regularity and downward-closed feasibility to unrelated economic environments.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper restricts an opaque distribution-sensitive mechanism problem to transparent auction classes and proves explicit approximation guarantees under declared distribution and feasibility conditions.
non_applicability: Do not use an approximation pivot when no formal loss metric exists or when simplicity is only computational convenience with no economic interpretation.
source_cards.title: Simple versus Optimal Mechanisms
source_cards.transferable_content: Use a bounded-loss simple class to expose the cutoff, monotonicity, or decomposition supporting most of the objective, while retaining the exact benchmark and every condition behind the guarantee.

source_cards.citation: Itai Ashlagi, Faidra Monachou, and Afshin Nikzad (2025), Optimal Allocation via Waitlists: Simplicity through Information Design, Review of Economic Studies 92(1):40-68
does_not_support: The paper does not establish universal optimality of waitlists or permit adding an information-design instrument that is absent from the researcher-owned environment.
source_cards.functional_summary: The paper first characterizes an unrestricted direct-mechanism optimum and then obtains an exact simple waitlist implementation through an explicit information-design instrument.
non_applicability: Do not transfer the simple implementation without its arrival process, information instrument, supermodularity, waiting cost, and maintained objective.
source_cards.title: Optimal Allocation via Waitlists: Simplicity through Information Design
source_cards.transferable_content: Treat exact simple implementation as the zero-loss boundary of a structure pivot and use the unrestricted optimum to identify the partition, cutoff, or statistic a transparent theorem must explain.
